To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
adversarial examples optimized to misclassify a classifier as a target class are more transferable if the source classifier is trained to be slightly robust to small magnitude perturbations.

(1) training a source classifier to be slightly robust improves the transferability between source and target classifiers of targeted adversarial examples, (2) the transferability improvement is observed for both class-targeted and feature-targeted attacks, (3) the improvement is observed even when the target classifier is a different type of architecture, such as a transformer, (4) the transferability of adversarial examples is improved even if the source classifier is only trained to be robust to small-magnitudes adversarial

1) training the source classifier with adversarial examples (i.e., robust training) improves the transferability and effectiveness of targeted attacks, 2) the robustness of the source classifier is not necessary for this improvement to occur, and 3) robust training is effective even when the adversarial examples are not optimized for transferability.
